excerpt: Easily install the very best desktop apps with the click of a button from Fedora's repositories, Flathub or anywhere else.
Flip a switch to turn on dark mode and give your eyes a break. Or use night light to reduce screen glare and help with sleep.
Optionally, bring your online calendar, contacts and data to the desktop with online accounts.
Boxes takes the guesswork out of using virtual machines. Just select the OS you want to install, and the app will do the rest.
Use performance mode to boost hardware speed when you need it. Turn off notifications with Do Not Disturb. Press the Super key and just type to search for what you need.
Use the latest container tools from the Red Hat ecosystem. No setup required. Access the Red Hat container registry.
All the packages, tools and runtimes you might need, up to date and ready for use with just a single command.
Easily install, update and manage software packages
I much prefer KDE over GNOME and with all recent enhancements to Plasma this is a very welcome change (short of KDE being the default).
I installed Fedora 40 KDE and it is fantastic. The UI is powerful but quite navigable. Features are fleshed out and accessible. Laptop and Wi-Fi features are top notch.
Libadwaita is a horrible design language. It wastes so much space, the disparity between gtk3/4 hurts the eyes and you pretty much depend on extensions for the most basic of things.
Interestingly, I've tried KDE multiple times on different devices & each time there's a Wifi issue that's not present in any other linux desktop.
Fedora 39 KDE Spin has been flawless so far, and I love the window tiling native support. Also, suspend on Nvidia works again for me.
I've tried a variety of linucies, but I keep coming back to Fedora. It frequently works the best 'out of the box'... My biggest complaint is nvidia's drivers, but that's not unique to Fedora.
I've tried, and honestly, on my low end hardware, only Arch seems to be the smoothest... Fedora always freezes for minutes when the RAM is full. I'm thinking maybe it's ZRAM fault here?

Unfortunately I cannot switch to Fedora on my desktop, mainly because of lack of support of Adobe (need for work), missing 10bit support and CUDA. Linux is not mature for professional work in audiovisual production.
My experience with Fedora ended quickly, after installing it in the VBox... every second letter of any text had been invisible and the whole DE was blinking... Went back to Ubuntu and Xubuntu.
Bought a Lenovo laptop for my daughter's school work... installed Fedora 39 on it. Everything just worked out of the box, got my Logi MX Master 3s configured and even touchpad gestures work!!!
I don't want to sound hypocritical, but I prefer good old linux distribution, without flatpaks, without strange immutability stuff... it's better to just switch to Arch.
Cool roadmap, but a focus on Flatpak basically turns me away... sandboxed software is nothing but trouble on the Linux desktop right now... It's death by a thousand papercuts with Flatpak.
A lot of excellent improvements to desktop Linux. Flatpaks have been awesome, its great seeing the community build on flathub... Pipewire has been a big step up.
First problem in Linux desktop OS: you download a flatpak... 'no application found'... the second I wanted discord or Spotify on fedora I had to go through a whole page of commands to do it.
Having used both on a regular basis, I hope they stick with GNOME. KDE is highly-configurable, which brings about a level of fun, but otherwise somewhat unpolished and at least a bit more buggy.
GNOME is my perfect DE. I love how it actively tries to stay out of my way... I have no interest in KDE. It looks a little too much like Windows for me.
The fact that you need extensions for something as simple as dock functionality is insane... all my extensions get broken for a month after every single release is downright infuriating.

I started using Fedora as my desktop just as they defaulted to wayland and honestly the transition has barely been noticed by me. The biggest issue a few years ago was screen sharing not working in Teams.
Please, please, please don't require Wayland yet. It's still not ready for prime time... It is going to reduce the ability for small window manager to innovate.
Arch just updated KDE to version 6 and has enabled Wayland by default. For some reason, mouse handling is just terrible... so I went back to Xorg.
